summary: Clearwater County steel CCC fire lookout in White Earth State Forest; lists disagree on 1934 vs 1935 and 80 vs 86 ft; listed as standing; ladder starts high.

facts.design: Steel tower with exterior ladder; Clearwater County list gives an International Derrick design with a square cab
facts.agency: Minnesota Forest Service, now Minnesota DNR Forestry Division

access.note: A visitor's account: a forest track appeared to reach the summit area, and the ladder starts high above the ground. No access rule found.

visit.trail_note: Visitor's account: a forest track appeared to reach the summit area. The visitor parked on a small road and went the last part on foot.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. Central US lookouts gives 1934 and 80 feet; the Clearwater County list gives 1935 and 86 feet. Not settled.

evidence.supports: 1934, 80-foot International Derrick steel tower with exterior ladder, built by the CCC
evidence.quote: 1934: A 80-foot International Derrick steel tower with an exterior ladder access constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: CCC tower standing in White Earth State Forest
evidence.quote: A CCC tower standing in White Earth State Forest off

evidence.supports: owner Minnesota Forest Service, now DNR Forestry Division
evidence.quote: Minnesota Forest Service, now Mn Department of Natural Resources, Forestry Division

evidence.supports: legal location 143N-38W-4 (township, range, section), not an agency
Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Height of Land as standing
evidence.quote: Height of Land Clearwater 47.23182 -95.50349 Tower Standing

evidence.supports: tower stands at the summit area; ladder starts well above ground, so climbing is not practical
evidence.quote: A large fire-lookout tower stands there, but the ladder begins well above the ground, so climbing it was not a practical option.

evidence.supports: forest track appeared to reach the summit area (visitor's observation)
evidence.quote: The forest track continued towards the summit, and on my visit it appeared to go essentially all the way up.

evidence.supports: visitor parked on the side of a small road
evidence.quote: I eventually squeezed onto the side of a small road, partly in the bushes and partly blocking it.

evidence.supports: visitor went the last part on foot, then ran

corrections.proposed: Minnesota Forest Service, now Minnesota DNR Forestry Division
corrections.why: 143N-38W-4 is a township, range and section (the legal land location), not an agency. The county list names the Minnesota Forest Service as owner.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Central US lookouts gives 1934 and 80 feet; the Clearwater County list gives 1935 and 86 feet (about 26.2 m). The record keeps 24.4 m (80 ft) from the first list. Not settled.

sources.title: A mosquito sprint to Height of Land Lookout

notes_for_editor: Two lists disagree on year and height (1934/80 ft vs 1935/86 ft). No staffing or fire history found. The access level 'public' rests on one visitor account and no official rule; check before publishing. Owner and legal-location fields in the record are the main fixes. Verification 2026-10-09: the P600 account was corrected (the writer parked on a small road and walked the last part; did not drive the track to the summit).
